mechanism.name: Rho/Ras GTPase cytoskeletal regulation of endothelial sprouting, tip cell behavior, and junctional integrity
mechanism.summary: Multiple program genes encode Rho/Ras GTPase regulators that directly control endothelial cytoskeletal dynamics, angiogenic sprouting, and junction stability. Tiam1 (Rac1 GEF) mediates Ras-Tiam1-Rac1-Pak1 signaling required for endothelial migration and barrier integrity. ARHGAP18 (RhoC GAP) is an endogenous negative regulator of angiogenesis that limits tip cell formation, stabilizes endothelial junctions, regulates microtubule stability, and mediates flow-dependent EC alignment—all consistent with postnatal vascular remodeling. RasGRP3 activates Ras-ERK signaling in developing blood vessels and regulates endothelial migration. Itga4 (integrin α4) participates in endothelial directional sprouting and migration. Additional Rho/Arf GAPs (Srgap2, Arap2) and scaffold proteins (Sorbs1) expand this cytoskeletal module. VEGFR2/Kdr as a perturbation regulator links growth factor signaling to this Ras/Rho axis.

mechanism.name: LMO2-ETS1 endothelial transcription factor network driving angiogenic remodeling and tip cell identity
mechanism.summary: Lmo2 and Ets1 are master endothelial transcription factors that together orchestrate angiogenic remodeling in postnatal development. LMO2 forms a complex with TAL1 to regulate VEGFR2, DLL4, and angiopoietin-2 specifically in tip cells during sprouting angiogenesis; Lmo2-null endothelial cells fail to contribute to angiogenic remodeling after embryonic day 10. ETS1 transduces VEGF signaling to globally promote RNA polymerase II pause release and drive angiogenesis; ETS1 loss reduces expression of Kdr, Cldn5, and other angiogenic genes in endothelial cells. The perturbation regulators Notch1 and Kdr intersect with this network: Notch1 variants disrupt hierarchical arterial-capillary-venous organization in brain vessels, and Kdr (VEGFR2) is a direct transcriptional target of ETS1. Additional TFs Zfp608 and Arid5b, and the Ras-Notch transducer Rasgrp3, likely expand this transcriptional module.

mechanism.name: Wnt/Norrin-Fzd4 and TGFβ/endoglin signaling for CNS vascular development and blood-brain barrier specification
mechanism.summary: The perturbation regulators Fzd4, Eng, and Tgfbr1 define a signaling axis that controls CNS vascular development and BBB integrity in postnatal brain. Norrin/Fzd4 canonical Wnt signaling is essential for postnatal retinal and brain vascular development and BBB/BRB maintenance; Fzd4 KO brain ECs are selectively eliminated from the vascular network. Wnt7a and Norrin systems partially overlap in CNS BBB maintenance. TGFβ receptor ALK5 (Tgfbr1) controls brain endothelial morphogenesis and BBB integrity: pericyte ALK5 drives TIMP3 to regulate EC morphogenesis in the developing brain, and ALK5/TGFβ signaling controls BBB permeability in brain ECs. Endoglin (Eng), an endothelial TGFβ co-receptor, is required for proper endothelial migration and arteriovenous patterning—its loss causes HHT with brain AVMs. Within the program genes, Quaking (Qk) supports endothelial cell cycle progression and angiogenic sprouting. Hmcn1 and Adamts5/12 likely contribute ECM remodeling support for vascular maturation.

mechanism.name: TGF-β/BMP-ALK signaling drives brain endothelial ECM production and BBB maturation
mechanism.summary: Brain endothelial cells in this program express a TGF-β/Wnt/β-catenin-regulated ECM gene set (Adamtsl2, Htra3) that has been directly identified in forebrain endothelial cells during neurovascular maturation. Htra3 provides extracellular TGF-β/BMP antagonism (feedback), while Skil/SnoN modulates intracellular TGF-β signaling by facilitating ALK1-Smad1/5 activity and repressing ALK5-Smad2/3, balancing pro-angiogenic versus barrier-promoting outputs. Tram2 (distinctive gene) supports type I collagen/ECM secretion via the ER translocon. The positive requirement for Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr2 (their KO reduces the program) is consistent with TGF-β signaling being a driver of this brain endothelial ECM/BBB maturation state.

mechanism.name: TGF-β/BMP-ALK signaling drives brain endothelial ECM production and BBB maturation
mechanism.summary: Brain endothelial cells in this program express a TGF-β/Wnt/β-catenin-regulated ECM gene set (Adamtsl2, Htra3) that has been directly identified in forebrain endothelial cells during neurovascular maturation. Htra3 provides extracellular TGF-β/BMP antagonism (feedback), while Skil/SnoN modulates intracellular TGF-β signaling by facilitating ALK1-Smad1/5 activity and repressing ALK5-Smad2/3, balancing pro-angiogenic versus barrier-promoting outputs. Tram2 (distinctive gene) supports type I collagen/ECM secretion via the ER translocon. The positive requirement for Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr2 (their KO reduces the program) is consistent with TGF-β signaling being a driver of this brain endothelial ECM/BBB maturation state.

evidence.relevance_note: Demonstrates Nrp1 suppresses stalk-cell phenotype by limiting Smad2/3 activation via ALK1/ALK5; Notch downregulates Nrp1 to drive stalk-cell behavior, directly linking Notch1, Nrp1, and TGF-β in endothelial tip/stalk specification
evidence.title: Alk1 and Alk5 inhibition by Nrp1 controls vascular sprouting downstream of Notch

mechanism.name: Notch1-Nrp1-Vezf1 axis controlling tip/stalk cell specification and brain endothelial identity
mechanism.summary: Nrp1 (neuropilin-1) suppresses the stalk-cell phenotype by limiting TGF-β/BMP signaling through ALK1 and ALK5; Notch1 downregulates Nrp1 to relieve this inhibition and drive stalk-cell behavior. This Notch1-Nrp1-TGF-β/BMP crosstalk axis integrates all three non-TGFβR perturbation regulators and the Skil/SnoN program gene into a coherent stalk/tip cell specification mechanism. Vezf1, an endothelial-specific zinc finger transcription factor, is expressed in human brain microvascular endothelial cells and regulates BBB-related genes (GLUT1, CLDN5), maintaining endothelial transcriptional identity. Ccm2 is required to prevent BMP6/TGF-β-driven EndMT in brain endothelial cells, thereby maintaining vascular identity against a pathological mesenchymal transition.

evidence.relevance_note: BBS9 is a core BBSome subunit; knockdown causes hydrocephaly, brain cilia loss, and reduced cilia number in zebrafish and mouse cells.
evidence.title: Knockdown of Bardet-Biedl syndrome gene BBS9/PTHB1 leads to cilia defects.

mechanism.name: Primary cilia biogenesis and ciliary trafficking via BBSome, IFT, and transition zone machinery
mechanism.summary: The largest coherent functional theme in P10 is cilia biogenesis and ciliary protein trafficking. Bbs9 encodes a core subunit of the BBSome complex, which mediates retrograde trafficking of GPCRs and other signaling receptors out of cilia via interaction with intraflagellar transport (IFT) complexes. Cc2d2a localizes to the ciliary transition zone and facilitates Rab8-dependent vesicle fusion at the ciliary base; mutations in CC2D2A cause Joubert and Meckel syndromes. Ift74 (together with Ift81) forms the principal module for IFT of tubulin into assembling cilia. Sdccag8 encodes a centrosomal/basal body protein whose C-terminal domain interacts with cilia length regulators Ick/Cilk1 and Mak; truncation causes polydactyly, cystic kidney, and retinal degeneration. Tbc1d32/Bromi acts at the ciliogenic basal body to regulate both Hedgehog transduction and early steps of ciliary bud formation. Cep164 is a distal appendage protein that organizes the platform for ciliary vesicle docking and IFT recruitment at the mother centriole. Nme7/NDK7 is a microtubule-binding nucleoside diphosphate kinase preferentially expressed in ciliated cells and identified as a cilia-associated gene candidate in zebrafish crispant screens. Wdpcp (a WD-repeat PCP effector) is essential for ciliogenesis in human epithelial cells. Cfap36 is a cilia- and flagella-associated protein (distinctive gene). Taken together, the majority of program and distinctive genes define a coherent cilia biogenesis and trafficking module.

evidence.relevance_note: Primary cilia on embryonic endothelial cells are required for full KLF2 shear stress response; cilia removal abolishes mechanosensitivity.

mechanism.name: Endothelial primary cilia as mechanosensors for blood flow in brain vasculature
mechanism.summary: Primary cilia on endothelial cells function as critical mechanosensors that detect fluid shear stress from blood flow and transduce it into intracellular signals. Endothelial cells bearing cilia are significantly more responsive to fluid shear stress (as measured by KLF2 induction) than non-ciliated cells; chemical removal of cilia abolishes this response. Primary cilia are found on endothelial cells in regions of low or disturbed flow, including in the embryonic and developing brain vasculature. In the context of postnatal brain vascular development, the cilia biogenesis genes of P10 (Bbs9, Cc2d2a, Wdpcp, Ift74, Nme7, Sdccag8, Tbc1d32, Cep164, Cfap36) would be required for endothelial cells to assemble functional primary cilia and thereby sense hemodynamic forces during network remodeling. WDPCP specifically modulates cilia beating via the MAPK/ERK pathway, connecting ciliary function to a major endothelial stress-signaling cascade. Thus the program's cilia genes likely underlie a mechanotransduction competency in postnatal brain endothelial cells.

evidence.relevance_note: Fzd4 is the Norrin receptor; loss causes BBB/BRB failure via cell-autonomous endothelial defects; gain causes premature vascular invasion.

mechanism.name: CNS angiogenesis and blood-brain barrier maintenance via Norrin/Wnt-Fzd4 signaling, GATA2, and Endoglin
mechanism.summary: The perturbation regulators of P10 — Fzd4, Gata2, and Eng — are three well-characterized drivers of brain endothelial identity and blood-brain barrier (BBB) function. Fzd4 (Frizzled-4) is the receptor for Norrin in canonical Wnt signaling and is essential for CNS vascular development and barrier integrity in the retina and cerebellum; its loss causes BBB/BRB breakdown through cell-autonomous mechanisms. Endoglin (Eng) is a TGF-β co-receptor specifically expressed on vascular endothelial cells; mutations cause hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia and haploinsufficiency elevates brain AVM risk, implicating it in cerebrovascular angiogenesis. GATA2 is a master endothelial transcription factor that controls endothelium-specific gene expression programs and epigenetic chromatin organization; it is also a regulator of endothelial HIF signaling and glycolytic adaptation. Tet1, a distinctive program gene, regulates DNA methylation dynamics in brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMVECs) and modulates angiogenic gene expression, placing it in the same epigenetic regulatory layer. Together these genes define a regulatory program governing CNS endothelial identity, postnatal BBB maturation, and angiogenic competence during brain development.

mechanism.name: Primary cilia biogenesis: basal body docking, transition zone integrity, intraflagellar transport, and BBSome assembly
mechanism.summary: The largest coordinated functional theme in P10 is the construction and maintenance of primary cilia. Multiple program genes encode core ciliary components: CC2D2A (Cc2d2a) and SDCCAG8 (Sdccag8) anchor the ciliary transition zone/diffusion barrier; CEP164 (Cep164) forms distal centriolar appendages that dock vesicles and recruit TTBK2 to initiate ciliogenesis; IFT74 (Ift74) partners with IFT81 to transport tubulin along the axoneme; BBS9 (Bbs9) is a structural subunit of the octameric BBSome that traffics membrane receptors into the cilium; WDPCP (Wdpcp) promotes cilia beating and is required for ciliogenesis; NME7 (Nme7) is an established ciliome member whose deletion causes primary ciliary dyskinesia; and TBC1D32/BROMI (Tbc1d32) is required for ciliogenesis and Hedgehog signaling through cilia. Distinctive genes reinforce this theme: IFT74, CEP164, and SDCCAG8 are archetypally ciliary, and CFAP36 (Cfap36) is annotated as a cilia-and-flagella-associated protein.

Multiple program genes encode core ciliary components: CC2D2A (Cc2d2a) and SDCCAG8 (Sdccag8) anchor the ciliary transition zone/diffusion barrier; CEP164 (Cep164) forms distal centriolar appendages that dock vesicles and recruit TTBK2 to initiate ciliogenesis; IFT74 (Ift74) partners with IFT81 to transport tubulin along the axoneme; BBS9 (Bbs9) is a structural subunit of the octameric BBSome that traffics membrane receptors into the cilium; WDPCP (Wdpcp) promotes cilia beating and is required for ciliogenesis; NME7 (Nme7) is an established ciliome member whose deletion causes primary ciliary dyskinesia; and TBC1D32/BROMI (Tbc1d32) is required for ciliogenesis and Hedgehog signaling through cilia. Distinctive genes reinforce this theme: IFT74, CEP164, and SDCCAG8 are archetypally ciliary, and CFAP36 (Cfap36) is annotated as a cilia-and-flagella-associated protein.

evidence.relevance_note: SDCCAG8 is a centrosomal/ciliopathy protein; its loss causes nephronophthisis and retinal degeneration with disrupted cilia-dependent signaling.
evidence.title: Renal-retinal ciliopathy gene Sdccag8 regulates DNA damage response signaling.

mechanism.name: Primary cilia mechanosensing and blood-brain barrier maturation in brain endothelial cells
mechanism.summary: In the specific cell-type context of brain endothelial cells, primary cilia serve as mechanosensors for blood-flow shear stress and as signaling organelles critical for postnatal blood-brain barrier (BBB) development. Reviews of brain vascular biology explicitly identify endothelial cilia as an emerging component of BBB genesis. Endothelial primary cilia in areas of low shear stress sensitize cells to fluid flow, amplifying the KLF2 shear response. Loss of ciliary function in vascular endothelial cells disrupts flow sensing, while manipulating ciliary length (rapamycin) alters mechanosensory sensitivity. The cilia/centrosome genes in P10 (Bbs9, Cc2d2a, Cep164, Ift74, Wdpcp, Nme7, Sdccag8, Tbc1d32, Cfap36) are thus collectively interpretable as supplying the ciliary apparatus needed for flow sensing and paracrine signaling during postnatal brain vascular maturation.

evidence.relevance_note: Identifies endothelial cilia biology as an emerging area in brain vascular patterning alongside Wnt signaling and neural-vascular crosstalk.
evidence.title: Established, New and Emerging Concepts in Brain Vascular Development.

mechanism.name: Wnt/Norrin-FZD4 signaling and endothelial identity regulators governing BBB and CNS vascular barrier formation
mechanism.summary: The perturbation regulators of P10 — FZD4, GATA2, and Endoglin (ENG) — define a distinct layer of transcriptional and receptor-mediated control over brain endothelial identity and BBB integrity. FZD4 is the obligate receptor for the Norrin/Wnt ligand in CNS vasculature; FZD4-deficient mice lose BBB function, and bioengineered FZD4-selective agonists restore BBB integrity after ischemic injury. GATA2 is a master endothelial transcription factor required for VEGF-driven sprouting angiogenesis and is de-repressed by injury to activate angiogenic programs. Endoglin (ENG) is an endothelial TGF-β co-receptor whose haploinsufficiency causes hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia with brain AVMs, and it modulates angiogenesis and vascular integrity through the ALK1/ALK5 axis. These three regulators collectively tune the transcriptional state of the brain endothelial cells in which the ciliary P10 gene program operates.

mechanism.name: Sprouting angiogenesis and tip cell identity in postnatal CNS vasculature
mechanism.summary: The program is anchored by canonical tip cell markers Angpt2 and Cxcr4, together with the Cdc42 effector Cdc42ep3 that operates downstream of the tip-cell regulator Nrp1 to drive filopodial formation. Single-cell transcriptomic studies of postnatal mouse brain endothelium directly identify these as tip-cell-enriched genes, and the regulator logic is consistent: Nrp1 KO decreases the program (required for tip cell identity), while Tek/Tie2 KO increases it (Ang1/Tie2 normally promotes vessel quiescence/stalk identity, so its loss shifts cells toward tip cell state). Gabarapl1 (distinctive) promotes EPC migration and angiogenesis. Hopx is enriched in intracranial arterial ECs, marking a protective, specialized brain-EC state.

mechanism.name: TGF-β/Tgfbr1 signaling specifying CNS endothelial tip cell identity and vascular maturation
mechanism.summary: Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr2 knockouts both strongly decrease this program (log2fc -0.86 and -0.77), indicating TGF-β receptor signaling is required to maintain it. A key mechanistic anchor is that CNS-specific 'diving' tip cells (D-tip cells) guiding deep vascular plexus formation have uniquely high TGF-β signaling, and endothelial-specific deletion of ALK5/Tgfbr1 prevents their identity acquisition and deep plexus formation. mechanism.name: Endothelial ion channel mechanosensing and membrane calcium signaling
mechanism.summary: Kcnj2 (Kir2.1, inward rectifier K+ channel) and Cacna1c (L-type Ca2+ channel) are expressed in brain capillary endothelial cells and mediate mechanosensory responses to blood flow. Kir2.1 in capillaries of electrically active tissues senses extracellular K+ to contribute to functional hyperemia, making this channel particularly relevant for neurovascular coupling in postnatal brain. The distinctive gene Jph1 (Junctophilin-1) bridges the plasma membrane to the sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum, creating Ca2+ microdomains at PM-SR junctions critical for ion channel regulation in vascular cells. Syt12 (Synaptotagmin-12, distinctive) and Rgs6 (regulator of G-protein signaling) further support membrane calcium trafficking and GPCR signal modulation in these cells.

mechanism.name: Angiogenic tip cell identity and filopodial guidance in postnatal brain vessels
mechanism.summary: Multiple program genes are co-enriched in endothelial tip cells leading sprouting capillaries during postnatal brain vascularization. Cxcr4 and Angpt2 are robustly identified as tip-cell-enriched transcripts by retinal and brain endothelial transcriptomics. Nrp1 (perturbation regulator, KO reduces program) acts cell-autonomously in brain tip cells, enabling CDC42 activation and filopodial protrusion—a function linked mechanistically to CDC42 effector proteins (Cdc42ep3). Notch-dependent suppression of Angpt2 in stalk cells further confirms that Angpt2 marks the tip cell state opposed to Notch-activated stalk identity.

mechanism.name: Dll4-Notch-CXCR4 axis coupling sprouting to arteriovenous specification
mechanism.summary: In postnatal mice, Dll4/Notch signaling couples endothelial tip cell sprouting to arterial fate acquisition by controlling CXCR4 expression; tip cells that activate Notch upregulate CXCR4 to migrate and connect to the developing arterial circulation. HOPX is specifically upregulated in intracranial (versus extracranial) arterial endothelial cells, consistent with an arterial-identity role in the brain. Nrp1 is positioned downstream of Notch as a pivot: Notch downregulates Nrp1, which shifts cells from tip to stalk via Alk1/Alk5 TGF-β signaling, thus linking the sprouting-to-arterial transition to TGF-β pathway balance.

mechanism.name: TGF-β/Angiopoietin-2 signaling axis for postnatal brain vascular integrity and remodeling
mechanism.summary: The perturbation regulators Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr2 (both with negative log2fc upon KO, reducing this program) maintain postnatal CNS vascular integrity: endothelial Tgfbr2 deletion in neonatal mice causes brain micro-hemorrhages and failure of the angiogenic front to invade deeper neural tissue. TGF-β signaling also represses Angpt2 (a program gene) in brain vessels; loss of TGF-β/Alk5 signaling in pericytes de-represses Angpt2, causing germinal matrix hemorrhage, suggesting program P11 marks a TGF-β-dependent remodeling state in which Angpt2 is tightly regulated. Nrp1 links the tip-stalk decision to TGF-β signaling by limiting Smad2/3 activation through Alk1/Alk5.

mechanism.name: Microsomal CYP-mediated oxidative metabolism: xenobiotic detoxification and fatty acid hydroxylation
mechanism.summary: P450 oxidoreductase (Por) is the obligate electron donor for all microsomal cytochrome P450 enzymes. In this program, Por provides electrons to Cyp2d40 (xenobiotic oxidation) and to the fatty acid ω-hydroxylases Cyp4a12a and Cyp4a12b (mouse orthologs of human CYP4A11). CYP4A enzymes catalyze ω-oxidation of long-chain fatty acids and are regulated by PPARα; their upregulation in fatty liver disease generates reactive lipid intermediates and contributes to oxidative stress and NAFLD pathogenesis. The co-expression of Por with multiple CYP family members defines a coherent microsomal mixed-function oxidase system active in pericentral hepatocytes.

mechanism.summary: A dense cluster of program genes and perturbation regulators converges on the full hepatic lipid-metabolic axis: fatty acid import (Slc27a2/FATP2), triglyceride esterification and storage (Dgat2), VLDL assembly and secretion (Mttp/Ldlr), and transcriptional control of de novo lipogenesis via the SREBP pathway (Insig1, Scap) and carbohydrate-responsive ChREBP (Mlxipl). The perturbation regulators of this program—particularly Insig1, Scap, Dgat2, and Mlxipl—are core effectors of hepatic lipid homeostasis whose perturbation most strongly shifts program activity in both young and aged conditions. Retsat (retinol saturase) generates 13,14-dihydroretinoic acid, an endogenous RXR ligand that couples retinoid signaling to PPAR/RXR-regulated lipid gene networks. This theme is directly relevant to MASLD pathogenesis.

mechanism.name: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation: ADP/ATP exchange and electron transport chain
mechanism.summary: Two program/distinctive genes anchor a mitochondrial energy-transduction theme: Slc25a31 (ANT4), a mitochondrial inner membrane ADP/ATP antiporter that exports newly synthesized ATP in exchange for cytosolic ADP, and Cox6a1, a nuclear-encoded subunit of cytochrome c oxidase (Complex IV) that catalyzes the terminal step of the electron transport chain. Liver expresses tissue-specific COX subunit isoforms (including Cox6a1) that tune OXPHOS capacity to hepatic metabolic demands. Hepatocyte mitochondrial function is impaired in aging and MASLD, and reduced OXPHOS contributes to the lipid overload phenotype.

mechanism.name: Mevalonate pathway and post-squalene cholesterol biosynthesis
mechanism.summary: Nearly every program and distinctive gene encodes a sequential enzyme in the mevalonate-to-cholesterol pathway. Acat2 and Hmgcs1 generate HMG-CoA from acetyl-CoA; Mvk, Pmvk and Mvd (distinctive genes) phosphorylate mevalonate to isopentenyl-PP; Idi1 isomerizes it; Fdps and Fdft1 condense units to squalene; Lss cyclises squalene to lanosterol; then Cyp51 (14α-demethylase), Tm7sf2, Msmo1, Nsdhl, Hsd17b7, Sc5d and Dhcr7 complete the post-lanosterol Bloch/Kandutsch-Russell routes to cholesterol. Acss2 supplies the acetyl-CoA substrate via acetate. Together these genes constitute the complete de novo cholesterol biosynthesis program in mouse hepatocytes.

mechanism.name: SCAP/INSIG1-SREBP2 sterol-sensing feedback control of the cholesterol synthesis gene program
mechanism.summary: The perturbation regulators Scap and Insig1 are the canonical sterol-sensing machinery that controls SREBP2 processing and thereby transcribes the entire cholesterol biosynthesis gene program. SCAP escorts SREBP2 from ER to Golgi for proteolytic activation; knockout of Scap reduces hepatic cholesterol synthesis by ~80%, explaining its strong negative perturbation effect on P21. Insig1 retains the SCAP-SREBP2 complex in the ER when sterols are sufficient; knockout of Insig1 therefore hyper-activates SREBP2 and upregulates cholesterol synthesis genes, consistent with the positive log2FC observed in P21. Ldlr (positive perturbation FC) provides the complementary uptake limb: its loss forces compensatory upregulation of de novo synthesis via SREBP2. This SCAP-INSIG1-LDLR triad is the master feedback circuit gating the P21 program activity in both young and aged hepatocytes.

mechanism.name: Coordinate hepatic lipid output: VLDL-triglyceride assembly coupled to de novo sterol synthesis
mechanism.summary: The perturbation regulators Dgat2 and Mttp control the final step of VLDL assembly and secretion: Dgat2 synthesises diacylglycerol/triglycerides for VLDL core loading, and Mttp transfers lipids onto ApoB. Their negative perturbation log2FC on P21 indicates that blocking VLDL-TG export attenuates the upstream cholesterol biosynthesis program. Literature shows these two are co-regulated with cholesterol synthesis in hepatocytes: cholesterol loading induces both Dgat2 and Mttp to package lipids for export, while VLDL secretion creates demand for hepatic cholesterol synthesis. In the context of MASLD/aging, impaired VLDL export (reduced Mttp/Dgat2 activity) leads to hepatic lipid accumulation and downregulates coordinated biosynthesis, linking this regulator pair to the core P21 program.

evidence.relevance_note: Cholesterol loading of primary hepatocytes increases DGAT2 and MTTP mRNA levels and VLDL-TG secretion, demonstrating direct coupling between intracellular cholesterol (product of P21 program) and VLDL assembly via Dgat2/Mttp.
evidence.title: Effect of cholesterol on lipogenesis and VLDL-TG assembly and secretion in goose primary hepatocytes.

mechanism.name: SREBP2–Scap–Insig1 transcriptional control of the mevalonate pathway

mechanism.name: Dysregulation of hepatic cholesterol synthesis in MASLD and liver aging
mechanism.summary: The mevalonate/cholesterol biosynthesis pathway is elevated in fatty liver (MASLD) and contributes to hepatic senescence during aging. SREBP1/2-driven sterol synthesis promotes steatosis, and mevalonate pathway activity directly induces cellular senescence via ERRα and mitochondrial dysfunction in liver. The perturbation regulators Dgat2 and Mttp — whose knockdown is the strongest activator of this program — connect triglyceride synthesis and VLDL-coupled cholesterol esterification (Acat2) to the sterol programme, suggesting that impaired VLDL export liberates free cholesterol and amplifies mevalonate pathway transcription.

mechanism.name: Carbohydrate-responsive hepatic de novo lipogenesis
mechanism.summary: Multiple program genes encode enzymes that convert glucose and fructose carbons into lipogenic building blocks: Khk phosphorylates fructose to fructose-1-phosphate, Pklr drives pyruvate production from glycolysis, Acly cleaves citrate to generate cytosolic acetyl-CoA, and Me1 supplies NADPH for reductive fatty acid synthesis. The master perturbation regulator Mlxipl (ChREBP) transcriptionally activates this entire DNL gene set in response to intracellular sugar signals, while Gckr regulates hepatic glucokinase activity and glucose flux into the pathway. This coordinated program is strongly implicated in MASLD pathogenesis through excess hepatic triglyceride accumulation.

mechanism.name: Hepatic xenobiotic detoxification and reactive aldehyde/ROS defense
mechanism.summary: A second coherent cluster consists of enzymes that defend hepatocytes against cytotoxic aldehydes, electrophiles, and ROS. Aldh2 oxidizes acetaldehyde and lipid-derived aldehydes (4-HNE) in mitochondria. Gstm7, Gstp1, and Gstp3 conjugate glutathione to electrophilic xenobiotics and lipid peroxidation products. Ugdh generates UDP-glucuronate for glucuronidation-based clearance. Cyb5r3 mediates NADH-dependent reduction at the outer mitochondrial membrane. Mt1 and Mt2 are inducible metal-binding proteins that scavenge ROS and heavy metals. Lias synthesizes lipoic acid, an essential mitochondrial antioxidant cofactor. This detoxification suite is relevant to hepatocyte resilience under the oxidative conditions of MASLD and aging.

mechanism.summary: A second coherent cluster consists of enzymes that defend hepatocytes against cytotoxic aldehydes, electrophiles, and ROS. Aldh2 oxidizes acetaldehyde and lipid-derived aldehydes (4-HNE) in mitochondria. Gstm7, Gstp1, and Gstp3 conjugate glutathione to electrophilic xenobiotics and lipid peroxidation products. Ugdh generates UDP-glucuronate for glucuronidation-based clearance. Cyb5r3 mediates NADH-dependent reduction at the outer mitochondrial membrane. Mt1 and Mt2 are inducible metal-binding proteins that scavenge ROS and heavy metals. Lias synthesizes lipoic acid, an essential mitochondrial antioxidant cofactor. This detoxification suite is relevant to hepatocyte resilience under the oxidative conditions of MASLD and aging.

mechanism.name: Lipid/sterol sensing and triglyceride synthesis regulation
mechanism.summary: A third cluster, dominated by perturbation regulators, controls the downstream storage of newly synthesized lipids and sterol homeostasis. Insig1 retains SREBP precursors in the ER under high-sterol conditions, gating VLDL secretion and hepatic cholesterol accumulation in MASH. Dgat2 catalyzes the final committed step of triglyceride synthesis and modulates SREBP-1 cleavage via ER phospholipid composition. Scap is the sterol-sensing escort for SREBP processing. Together these regulators couple the acetyl-CoA produced by Acly to downstream sterol and TG synthesis, coordinating lipid output with cellular sterol status—a balance disrupted in both MASLD and aging.

mechanism.name: Pericentral (zone 3) xenobiotic and drug metabolism
mechanism.summary: Cyp2e1 and Cyp4b1 are cytochrome P450 enzymes that define pericentral (zone 3) hepatocytes and catalyze phase I oxidative metabolism of xenobiotics, drugs, and ethanol. Mgst1 provides complementary phase II glutathione conjugation of electrophilic metabolites, protecting against oxidative damage. Ces1d (carboxylesterase 1d) hydrolyzes ester-bond-containing xenobiotics and drugs. This pericentral xenobiotic gene cluster is under Wnt/β-catenin signaling control that establishes zone 3 identity. In aging and MASLD, disruption of this pericentral metabolic niche underlies heightened hepatotoxicity susceptibility.

mechanism.name: Peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid droplet dynamics
mechanism.summary: Acox1 (acyl-CoA oxidase 1) catalyzes the rate-limiting step of peroxisomal β-oxidation and is a key PPARα target; its loss accelerates NAFLD progression. Fitm1 (FIT1) is an ER-resident protein essential for lipid droplet biogenesis in liver. Ces1d hydrolyzes stored triglycerides in hepatocytes, linking lipid droplet turnover to oxidation. Pon1 is synthesized in the liver and associated with HDL-mediated reverse cholesterol transport; its activity is suppressed in hepatic steatosis. Chpt1 synthesizes phosphatidylcholine, critical for VLDL assembly and lipid export. Together these genes control hepatic lipid partitioning between storage, oxidation, and export—a balance disrupted in MASLD and aging.

mechanism.name: SREBP-driven lipogenesis and sterol biosynthesis suppressed by hepatokines Mup10/17
mechanism.summary: Perturbation regulators Srebf1 (SREBP1c), Scap, and Sqle form a lipogenic/cholesterogenic axis in hepatocytes: SCAP escorts SREBP1 to Golgi for cleavage, activating lipogenic genes including SQLE (rate-limiting cholesterol synthesis enzyme) and Dgat2. This axis is amplified in MASLD and aged liver. Mup10 and Mup17 are liver-derived hepatokines that suppress this lipogenic program—MUP1 inhibits gluconeogenic and lipogenic gene expression in hepatocytes, and MUP levels fall markedly in NAFLD/ER stress, removing a brake on lipogenesis. Pparg amplifies lipid uptake. This mechanism frames the program as a hepatocyte-intrinsic lipogenic regulatory module whose balance is eroded in aging and MASLD.

mechanism.name: Periportal amino acid catabolism and urea cycle nitrogen disposal
mechanism.summary: Multiple genes in this program converge on periportal hepatocyte catabolism of amino acids and disposal of resulting nitrogen via the urea cycle. Hal and Uroc1 catabolize histidine; Sds converts serine to pyruvate; Gls2 hydrolyzes glutamine releasing ammonia; Uox degrades purines; Cps1 is the rate-limiting urea cycle enzyme that fixes NH3 into carbamoyl phosphate; Sfxn1 transports serine into mitochondria supporting one-carbon flux linked to nitrogen handling; Rida processes reactive deaminated intermediates. These enzymes are classically co-expressed in the periportal zone and are downregulated together in NAFLD/MASLD and modulated by aging-related O-GlcNAcylation.

Hal and Uroc1 catabolize histidine; Sds converts serine to pyruvate; Gls2 hydrolyzes glutamine releasing ammonia; Uox degrades purines; Cps1 is the rate-limiting urea cycle enzyme that fixes NH3 into carbamoyl phosphate; Sfxn1 transports serine into mitochondria supporting one-carbon flux linked to nitrogen handling; Rida processes reactive deaminated intermediates. These enzymes are classically co-expressed in the periportal zone and are downregulated together in NAFLD/MASLD and modulated by aging-related O-GlcNAcylation.

evidence.relevance_note: Wnt/β-catenin suppresses HAL and ARG1 in liver cells via CEBPA/FOXA1, elevating histidine and arginine and disrupting urea cycle metabolite levels
evidence.title: Wnt/β-catenin signaling regulates amino acid metabolism through the suppression of CEBPA and FOXA1 in liver cancer cells.

mechanism.name: Hepatic gluconeogenesis and periportal glucose output regulated by insulin signaling
mechanism.summary: Pck1 (PEPCK1) is the rate-limiting gluconeogenic enzyme in periportal hepatocytes; Sds feeds pyruvate as gluconeogenic substrate; Gls2-derived α-ketoglutarate also enters gluconeogenesis. The insulin receptor (Insr) and its substrate Irs1 suppress Pck1 transcription postprandially; insulin resistance in aging and MASLD causes excess hepatic glucose production. Pck1 also phosphorylates INSIG1/2 (a young-condition perturbation regulator) at the ER, linking gluconeogenesis to SREBP-mediated lipogenesis and potentially contributing to MASLD steatosis.

evidence.title: Regulation of human hepatic hydroxysteroid sulfotransferase gene expression by the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha transcription factor.

mechanism.name: Hepatocyte steroid, bile acid, and xenobiotic sulfation/hydroxysteroid metabolism
mechanism.summary: Sult2a2 (hydroxysteroid sulfotransferase) sulfonates bile acids, hydroxysteroids, and procarcinogen xenobiotics in hepatocytes and is regulated by PPARα, a key lipid-sensing nuclear receptor activated in MASLD. Hsd17b6 is a 3α-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase expressed almost exclusively in hepatocytes that catalyzes androgen synthesis and is correlated with fatty liver disease, though its direct causal role in MASLD is dispensable in isolation. Slco1b2 (a perturbation regulator) encodes the hepatic organic anion transporter OATP1B2 that mediates uptake of bile acids and other conjugated substrates channeled to sulfation. Together, these genes represent hepatocyte-specific steroid/bile acid/xenobiotic processing capacity that is perturbed in MASLD.

mechanism.name: Hepatic Phase I/II xenobiotic detoxification and steroid/bile acid conjugation
mechanism.summary: The program encodes a comprehensive hepatic detoxification apparatus spanning Phase I oxidoreduction (Cyp2c50, Akr1c6, Aldh1a1, Aldh3a2) and Phase II conjugation (Gsta3, Sult2a5, Sult2a7, Sult2a8). The three SULT2A paralogs catalyze bile acid and steroid sulfation to enhance their solubility and biliary/urinary elimination. Aldh1a1 and Aldh3a2 oxidize reactive aldehydes arising from lipid peroxidation and xenobiotic metabolism. Gsta3 combines glutathione conjugation with steroid isomerase activity. This ensemble is characteristic of pericentral hepatocytes that execute high-throughput chemical detoxification and is altered both in hepatic aging and in MASLD/NASH. Perturbation regulators Tpst1 (sulfation of tyrosine residues) and Insig1 (sterol sensing, regulates bile acid feedback) are functionally aligned with this theme.

evidence.relevance_note: Establishes FITM1/Fitm1 as an ER-resident triglyceride-binding protein that directly partitions TG into lipid droplets; overexpression in mouse liver drives LD accumulation.
evidence.title: Direct binding of triglyceride to fat storage-inducing transmembrane proteins 1 and 2 is important for lipid droplet formation.

mechanism.name: Lipid droplet biogenesis and peroxisomal/ER fatty acid catabolism
mechanism.summary: A second coherent theme involves the formation of lipid droplets and the peroxisomal/ER catabolism of fatty acids. Fitm1 (FITM1) is an ER-resident transmembrane protein that directly binds triglyceride to partition it into lipid droplets. Hao2 is a peroxisomal hydroxy-acid oxidase involved in glyoxylate and short/medium-chain hydroxy-fatty acid oxidation. Eci2 encodes a peroxisomal enoyl-CoA delta isomerase required for beta-oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids. Cyb5b is an ER cytochrome b5 that donates electrons for fatty acid desaturation. Aldh3a2 (fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase) converts toxic fatty aldehydes generated during peroxisomal/microsomal lipid oxidation. Lonp2 is the peroxisomal Lon protease responsible for degrading oxidized or misfolded peroxisomal matrix proteins. The aggregate function is hepatic lipid homeostasis—coordinating lipid droplet loading, peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and ER fatty acid remodeling—processes that are directly dysregulated in MASLD. Regulators Dgat2 (triglyceride synthesis) and Abcg5 (biliary sterol secretion) define the boundaries of this lipid flux.

mechanism.name: Sulfur amino acid catabolism and nitrogen/ammonia detoxification (urea cycle support)
mechanism.summary: A third mechanism centers on hepatic sulfur amino acid catabolism and nitrogen disposal. Cdo1 (cysteine dioxygenase 1) is the gate-keeping enzyme that irreversibly oxidizes cysteine to cysteine sulfinic acid, committing it to taurine synthesis (for bile acid conjugation) or to sulfate/pyruvate. Cdo1 expression is regulated by bile acid/FXR signaling and its hepatocyte-specific deletion increases GSH capacity and protection from oxidative stress. Car5a (carbonic anhydrase VA, highly liver-enriched) supplies bicarbonate to carbamoylphosphate synthetase 1, the rate-limiting urea cycle enzyme for ammonia detoxification; Car5a knockout mice show impaired ureagenesis. Agmat (agmatinase) catabolizes agmatine to putrescine + urea, feeding into polyamine synthesis from arginine. Together these genes support the hepatic capacity to safely dispose of nitrogen and sulfur from amino acid catabolism. Aging regulator G6pc (glucose-6-phosphatase) is co-expressed in this periportal metabolic zone, and Insr regulates urea cycle enzyme activities via insulin signaling.

mechanism.name: Phase I/II xenobiotic, steroid, and bile acid detoxification (Nrf2/CAR-regulated hepatocyte program)
mechanism.summary: Multiple program genes encode consecutive enzymatic steps that oxidise, reduce, and conjugate endogenous steroids, bile acids, and xenobiotics. Sult2a5, Sult2a7, and Sult2a8 are bile acid/steroid sulfotransferases that sulfate hydroxy-bile acids and DHEA-like steroids to render them excretable. Gsta3 conjugates electrophilic substrates to glutathione (phase II), Akr1c6 performs ketone/aldehyde reductions (phase I), Aldh1a1 oxidises reactive aldehydes, and Cyp2c50 is a cytochrome P450 oxidase—all induced together by the Nrf2 transcription factor in mouse liver. Cyb5b supplies electrons to CYP450s and the outer-mitochondrial amidoxime reductase system for xenobiotic detoxification. The CAR nuclear receptor coordinately up-regulates Sult2a1-type enzymes together with the Mrp4 bile acid sulfate exporter as a cholestasis-protective mechanism. Perturbation regulator Abcg5 (ABC transporter for biliary cholesterol/sterol excretion) is likewise a direct Nrf2 target, connecting sterol detoxification flux to excretion.

mechanism.name: Peroxisomal and microsomal fatty acid catabolism and lipid aldehyde detoxification
mechanism.summary: A second cluster of program genes collectively executes peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and clears toxic lipid-derived aldehydes. Hao2 (HAOX2) is a peroxisomal 2-hydroxy acid oxidase expressed predominantly in liver that oxidises 2-hydroxy fatty acids as part of the alpha-oxidation pathway. Eci2 is the enoyl-CoA isomerase required to handle double bonds at odd-numbered positions during beta-oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids, with both mitochondrial and peroxisomal isoforms in liver. Aldh3a2 (FALDH, fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase) converts long-chain fatty aldehydes released during peroxisomal alpha-oxidation or lipid peroxidation to fatty acids; it is expressed in liver microsomes, regulated by insulin, and protects against lipid-derived oxidative stress. Fitm1 is an ER-resident transmembrane protein that directly binds triglyceride and partitions it into lipid droplets. Lonp2 (a peroxisomal Lon-type protease) maintains quality control of peroxisomal enzymes. Perturbation regulators Dgat2 (triglyceride synthesis) and Flcn (mTORC1/peroxisome biogenesis) modulate flux through this oxidative axis.

evidence.relevance_note: Identifies CDO1 as the rate-limiting enzyme of the cysteine→taurine shunt in mouse liver; taurine drives cholesterol excretion; LRRC58 E3-ligase controls CDO1 protein stability—establishes CDO1 as key hepatic metabolic regulator
evidence.title: Covariation MS uncovers a protein that controls cysteine catabolism.

mechanism.name: Hepatic cysteine catabolism, taurine biosynthesis, and sulfur amino acid homeostasis
mechanism.summary: Cdo1, a program gene and among the most hepatocyte-enriched enzymes, is the rate-limiting enzyme converting cysteine to cysteine sulfinic acid—the entry point for taurine synthesis and a major determinant of hepatic cysteine availability, GSH production, and cholesterol handling. Bile acid/FXR signalling represses CDO1, tightly coupling sulfur amino acid flux to the bile acid cycle. CDO1 activity also controls gluconeogenesis by limiting hepatic cysteine (knockdown of CDO1 raises liver cysteine and glucose output; PMID 39819116), linking it to perturbation regulator G6pc (glucose-6-phosphatase). Agmat (agmatinase, a distinctive gene) catalyses agmatine hydrolysis in the urea/polyamine pathway, and Car5a (mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase V) supplies HCO3⁻ for carbamoyl phosphate synthetase in ureagenesis—both extending the nitrogen/amine detoxification axis. Rgn/SMP30, a program gene, is a calcium-binding protein that declines progressively with aging in hepatocytes, directly matching the aging condition of this program. Sord (sorbitol dehydrogenase) participates in polyol/fructose metabolism in liver and is co-regulated with NRF2 target genes under metabolic stress. Perturbation regulators Insr and G6pc converge on the glucose–amino acid homeostasis nexus that CDO1 participates in.
